title: Enterprise visibility recalculation freeze: 4-stage Sharing Architecture refactor

stages.scenario: A multinational financial services enterprise with 3 million Accounts experiences cascading row-lock failures (`UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW`) and 6-hour system-wide recalculation freezes whenever territory alignments occur. Inspection reveals an 11-level role hierarchy and 180 criteria-based sharing rules granting access across regional branches. What is the fundamental platform bottleneck?

options.text: Deep role hierarchies amplify implicit sharing tree traversal exponentially; modifying a high-level node or criteria-based sharing rule locks the entire UserRole and Group sharing tables to rebuild millions of share rows.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! According to the Platform Sharing Architecture guide, deep hierarchies (> 4-5 levels) and proliferation of criteria-based sharing rules trigger massive implicit sharing recalculations, causing systemic table locking on AccountShare.

options.text: Criteria-based sharing rules are limited to a maximum of 20 rules per object across all editions.
options.coachingFeedback: False limit: Salesforce allows up to 300 criteria-based sharing rules per object (50 criteria-based in Enterprise), but using them heavily on large data volumes causes severe recalculation overhead.

options.text: The platform requires all 3 million Accounts to be assigned to a single default system administrator role.
options.coachingFeedback: Antipattern: Assigning millions of records to a single user or role creates catastrophic ownership skew and lock contention on record updates.

stages.scenario: To redesign this sharing architecture for enterprise scale and eliminate long recalculation freezes, what target pattern does the Platform Sharing Architecture guide prescribe?

options.text: Flatten the role hierarchy to 3–4 executive levels, shift regional branch visibility to Account Teams with programmatic provisioning, and replace broad criteria-based sharing with Restriction Rules or Scoping Rules for sensitive data filtering.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! The Platform Sharing Architecture fundamentals guide recommends flattening the hierarchy, using granular Account Teams to localize share recalculations, and leveraging Restriction/Scoping Rules to control record visibility without rebuilding the share table.

options.text: Set Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD) to Public Read/Write on Account and enforce data privacy using validation rules.
options.coachingFeedback: Severe antipattern: Validation rules only block edit/save operations and cannot prevent unauthorized data reads, reports, API queries, or list view exposure, violating the Trust pillar.

stages.scenario: How should the enterprise safely execute the transition from the legacy 11-level hierarchy and criteria rules to the flattened architecture without locking active production transactions?

options.text: Leverage 'Defer Sharing Calculation' in Setup to suspend automatic rule processing, restructure roles and Account Teams during a scheduled maintenance window, and then trigger asynchronous background recalculation.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! The Platform Sharing Architecture guide recommends enabling Deferred Sharing Calculation for major structural reorganizations so role hierarchy and sharing changes can be applied in bulk without intermediate locks.

options.text: Delete old roles directly during business hours while users are actively logging in to allow real-time redistribution.
options.coachingFeedback: Antipattern: Deleting and reassigning roles during peak hours creates immediate deadlocks on Group and Share tables, locking out users.

stages.scenario: What observability mechanism should be put in place to ensure sharing recalculations remain within healthy thresholds post-cutover?

options.text: Subscribe to Real-Time Event Monitoring for URI and ApexExecution events tracking share recalculation duration, and monitor the Background Jobs page for asynchronous share maintenance throughput.
options.coachingFeedback: Correct! Event Monitoring and Background Jobs telemetry allow architects to track asynchronous job queue latency and verify that recalculations finish within SLA windows.

options.text: Rely on user complaints about missing records on their dashboard to indicate sharing issues.
options.coachingFeedback: Antipattern: Relying on end-user complaints represents a lack of operational observability and risks latent data exposure or access revocation.
